footer.aboutTitle: About This Quick Human Anatomy Quiz
footer.topicText: This short quiz covers familiar body facts across organs, bones, muscles, blood, breathing, digestion, senses, and anatomy terms.
footer.aboutText: The questions are built to feel like fast pub-quiz trivia, with clear body facts and short explanations after the result. It is made for general knowledge, entertainment, and self-challenge only. It is not medical advice, diagnosis, professional training, or a clinical assessment. If you have health concerns, speak to a qualified healthcare professional.

questions.prompt: Which organ never really gets a day off pumping blood?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood through vessels so oxygen and nutrients can travel around the body.

questions.prompt: Which bony shield protects your brain?
questions.explanation: The skull is the bony case that protects the brain.

questions.prompt: Which muscle quietly helps every breath happen?
questions.explanation: The diaphragm contracts and relaxes to help air move in and out of the lungs.

questions.prompt: How many chambers are working inside the human heart?
questions.explanation: The human heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles.

questions.prompt: Which organs do the heavy lifting when you take in oxygen?
questions.explanation: The lungs bring oxygen into the body and help remove carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: Which organ is the body's command center?
questions.explanation: The brain controls thoughts, movement, senses, and many body functions.

questions.prompt: Which organ produces enzymes that help digest food?
questions.explanation: The pancreas makes enzymes that help break down food during digestion.

questions.prompt: Which part of the eye controls how much light enters?
questions.explanation: The pupil changes size to let more or less light into the eye.

questions.prompt: Which valve-like flap helps stop food going down the windpipe?
questions.explanation: The epiglottis helps cover the windpipe when you swallow.

questions.prompt: Which term means closer to the head?
questions.explanation: Superior means toward the head or upper part of the body.
